record.context_brief: Exponential upper bound on flow complexity
record.original_question: For a geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) on a compact two-dimensional manifold, with absolute complexity C defined via products of small exponential-map neighborhoods of the identity, can one prove that C(gamma(t)) is bounded above exponentially in time by a constant of the form exp(t||dot gamma(0)||_{H^s})?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary), and for $s > 2$ let $\mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving Sobolev $H^s$-diffeomorphisms of $M$, equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric whose geodesics correspond (via Arnold's formalism) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Near the identity $e \in \mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$, fix a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ which lies in the image of the Riemannian exponential map at $e$. For any $\varphi \in \mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$, define the absolute complexity
$$C(\varphi) := \min\{ k \in \mathbb{N} : \varphi = \varphi_1 \varphi_2 \cdots \varphi_k \text{ with each } \varphi_i \in U \},$$
i.e., the minimal number of factors from $U$ needed to express $\varphi$ as a product.

Let $\gamma : [0,T) \to \mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$ be a geodesic of the $L^2$ metric starting at $\gamma(0) = e$ with initial velocity $\dot{\gamma}(0) \in T_e \mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $K > 0$ (depending only on $M$ and the chosen neighborhood $U$) such that for all $t \ge 0$ in the interval of existence,
$$C(\gamma(t)) \le K \exp\!\big(t \, \|\dot{\gamma}(0)\|_{H^s}\big).$$
artifact.category_tag: Diffeomorphism group geodesics and Euler equations
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of the open problems in a 2022 survey on geometric hydrodynamics, where it is stated that establishing such an exponential bound on complexity along geodesics in the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group would imply the classical double-exponential growth estimate for solutions of the 2D Euler equations. No resolution appears in the literature; the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: A collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics, including a problem asking to prove that complexity C(gamma(t)) of a geodesic in the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group of a 2D manifold grows at most exponentially in time.
status_evidence.claim: The exponential complexity bound for geodesics in D_mu^s(M) is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems (Khesin et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem asks to show C(gamma(t)) is bounded by exp(t||dot gamma(0)||_{H^s}), which would imply the double exponential estimate for the Euler equations.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented without a known proof.
